players.product: E-Infrastructure site development (earthwork, grading, site utilities) and CEC electrical construction for hyperscale data-center and semiconductor campuses

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 revenue growth of 90% and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 116%, from $2.69 to $5.80; adjusted EBITDA more than doubled with margins up 150 basis points to 22%. 'The current market demand allows us to be selective.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue +90% YoY; adj. diluted EPS $5.80 (+116%); adj. EBITDA margin 22%

quarterly_data.signal: Signed backlog $4.3 billion (+116% YoY, +50% organic); combined backlog $5.6 billion (+150%); high-probability future-phase opportunities exceed $1.4 billion, so the total addressable pool of work is more than $7 billion, up more than $2.5 billion since year-end. Q2 book-to-burn 1.4x on backlog and 1.3x on combined backlog ex-StoneRidge.
quarterly_data.figure: signed backlog $4.3B (+116% YoY); combined backlog $5.6B (+150%); total pool of work >$7B; book-to-burn 1.4x

quarterly_data.signal: E-Infrastructure revenue grew 192% with data centers and semiconductor campuses the primary driver; adjusted operating income +148% at a 24% margin. Mission-critical work (data centers, large manufacturing, semiconductor) was more than 92% of E-Infrastructure signed backlog; E-Infrastructure signed backlog plus unsigned electrical awards plus future-phase site work now exceeds $6 billion, up $2.7 billion since year-end.
quarterly_data.figure: E-Infrastructure revenue +192%; adj. operating margin 24%; mission-critical >92% of signed backlog; E-Infra backlog + awards + future phase >$6B

quarterly_data.signal: CEC (electrical) revenue +140% YoY; CEC combined backlog rose $1.7 billion since year-end 2025 to about $2.4 billion, and 'CEC is now getting the second buildings on data centers that they're at'. CEC capacity filled in about 90 days after acquisition; Q2 adjusted margin 11.4% vs upper-20s for site development, with 300-500 basis points of CEC margin improvement targeted over 12-18 months. 'If we had 1,000 or 2,000 more electricians, we'd be growing it even faster.'
quarterly_data.figure: CEC revenue +140% YoY; CEC combined backlog ~$2.4B (+$1.7B since year-end 2025); CEC adj. margin 11.4%

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance raised: revenue $4 billion-$4.15 billion, adjusted diluted EPS $19.70-$20.30, adjusted EBITDA $891 million-$916 million (midpoints = 64% revenue growth, 84% adjusted EPS growth). E-Infrastructure segment revenue growth over 100% including CEC and StoneRidge, legacy site development approaching 70% or higher, E-Infrastructure adjusted operating margin in the mid 20% range. Q3 awards may be softer on timing with higher awards in Q4 and early 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $4B-$4.15B; adj. EPS $19.70-$20.30; adj. EBITDA $891M-$916M; E-Infrastructure revenue growth >100%

quarterly_data.signal: CapEx guidance raised by $30 million to $130 million-$140 million for fleet capacity and productivity; Rocky Mountain division revenue up nearly 700% as it shifts from transportation to E-Infrastructure data-center work; StoneRidge acquisition ($140 million signed backlog) positions for Pacific Northwest activity in late 2027-2028. Revolver upsized to $1.5 billion for capacity-adding M&A.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 CapEx guidance $130M-$140M (+$30M); Rocky Mountain revenue +700%; StoneRidge signed backlog ~$140M; revolver $1.5B

quarterly_data.signal: Hyperscaler demand visibility: 'What we are seeing just from our top hyperscalers, the amount of work that is coming, we have to add capacity significantly faster just to keep up with them.' Customers are purchasing incremental land adjacent to existing campuses; projects that were three years are now five to eight to 12 years, none of which is in future-phase numbers. Texas 'is going to be bigger in the next three years than any other market related to data centers'. Electricians remain the tightest resource; no schedule delays from data-center moratorium politics seen.

Semiconductor campus: the Northeast semiconductor project is running ahead of schedule with significant Q3 revenue expected, positioning Sterling 'as the go-to solution for large, complex projects' in semis; next wave of semiconductor plants seen around 2030, pharma 2028; initial scope awarded on an EV plant outside Atlanta.
